items.title: Iran demands Lebanon be included in any ceasefire deal

featured_image.name: Iran rejects US ceasefire plan, issues its own demands as strikes land  across the Mideast | 830 WCCO

items.description:
Iran has told intermediaries that Lebanon must be part of any ceasefire agreement with the United States and Israel, linking an end to the nearly month-long war to a halt in Israel's military campaign against Hezbollah, according to a Reuters report citing six regional sources familiar with Tehran's position.[1][2]

The demand, communicated to mediators as early as mid-March, adds a layer of complexity to nascent and indirect diplomatic exchanges between Washington and Tehran as the conflict approaches its fourth week with no clear path to resolution.

items.title: UK authorizes military to board Russian shadow fleet tankers

featured_image.name: UK to authorize military seizure of shadow fleet tankers evading Russia oil  sanctions

items.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on Wednesday that he has given the military and law enforcement agencies permission to board and detain Russian shadow fleet vessels in British waters, escalating the United Kingdom's campaign to cut off oil revenues funding Moscow's war in Ukraine.[1][2]

The decision marks the first time the UK has authorized its own forces to directly intercept the sanctioned tankers, after months of supporting allied operations led by the United States and France. Starmer framed the move as a response to rising oil prices driven by the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran, warning that Russian President Vladimir Putin was "rubbing his hands" at the prospect of higher energy revenues.[3][1]

items.title: Iran’s expanding long-range missiles pose growing threat

items.description: Nearly four weeks into the U.S.-Israeli air campaign against Iran, Tehran continues to launch ballistic missiles at Israel and Gulf states despite what both Washington and Jerusalem describe as a devastating degradation of its military capabilities. items.title: 2,600-year-old shipwreck yields oldest known raw iron cargo

featured_image.name: Iron from a 2,600-year-old shipwreck off Israeli coast may ...

items.description:
Researchers at the University of Haifa announced Wednesday that an underwater excavation off Israel's northern Mediterranean coast has uncovered what they describe as the earliest known seaborne shipment of raw iron, dating back roughly 2,600 years. The nine chunks of unprocessed iron, known as "blooms," were recovered from a shipwreck in the Dor Lagoon near the Carmel Coast and published in the peer-reviewed journal Heritage Science, part of the Nature group.[1][2][3][4]

The discovery challenges long-held assumptions about how iron moved through ancient trade networks. Scholars had generally believed that iron was smelted and immediately hammered into finished billets at production sites. The Dor Lagoon blooms show no signs of forging or further processing, indicating they were shipped in their raw, as-smelted state to be worked elsewhere.[2][4]

items.title: Russia finalizing large aid shipment to Iran with drones and supplies

featured_image.name: What we know and do not know about the Iran war negotiations

items.description:
Russia is close to completing a phased shipment of drones, medicine, and food to Iran, according to Western intelligence reports first detailed by the Financial Times on Wednesday, marking the clearest evidence yet that Moscow is providing direct military support to Tehran as the US-Israeli campaign enters its fourth week.[1][2]

The shipments follow negotiations between senior Russian and Iranian officials that began in early March, just days after the United States and Israel launched coordinated strikes on Iran on February 28. The drone deliveries represent a dramatic escalation of Russian involvement in the conflict, moving beyond intelligence sharing to tangible military hardware.[1]

items.title: US says it has struck 10,000 targets in Iran over 26 days

featured_image.name: Navy Adm. Brad Cooper takes over at CENTCOM

items.description:
US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper announced on Wednesday that American forces have struck more than 10,000 Iranian military targets over 26 days of Operation Epic Fury, claiming the destruction of 92% of Iran's largest naval vessels and more than two-thirds of the country's missile, drone, and naval production facilities and shipyards.[1][2]

Cooper, in his fifth video update on the campaign posted to X, said the milestone of 10,000 targets had been reached "just hours ago" and that the operation remains "on plan or ahead of plan" in achieving its military objectives. "My operational assessment is they have now lost the ability to meaningfully project naval power and influence around the region and around the world," Cooper said.[2][1]

items.title: Netanyahu orders 48-hour blitz on Iran amid ceasefire fears

featured_image.name: Netanyahu to discuss potential Iran strikes with Trump as ...

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday night ordered military commanders to destroy as much of Iran's weapons manufacturing capacity as possible within 48 hours, according to a New York Times report cited by i24 News, as fears grew within the Israeli government that President Donald Trump could announce ceasefire negotiations at any moment.[1]

The directive came after Israel received a copy of a 15-point American peace proposal transmitted to Iran through Pakistani intermediaries. Netanyahu issued the order following briefings from the commanders of the Israeli Air Force and the Intelligence Directorate on remaining targets that could still be struck, according to two official Israeli sources.[2][1]
